head: 9df83c38
note: Pseudo-code written by the reviewing agent; explain_check.py verifies every step against the cited lines.

steps.text: a library source defines a struct `MyGenericStruct<T>` marked `[MessagePackObject]` with one member `[Key(0)]` `T Content`
an app source has a class `MyObject` with a `[Key(0)]` member of type `MyGenericStruct<int>`, plus a resolver `MyResolver` marked `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver]`
the helper first compiles the library source into a separate assembly `DefiningProject` and gives it to the app only as a metadata reference (no source)
the analyzers and generator run on the app with no expected diagnostics, so any diagnostic fails the test (the comment names the crash signs `AD0001` and `CS8785`)
a second, direct generator run must report nothing at `DiagnosticSeverity.Warning` or above (`Assert.Empty`) and its output must include a file named `expectedResolverHintName` (`Assert.Contains`)

does_not_check: It does not check the content of the generated code, or that the closed generic member serializes at run time.
It does not cover the case the new diagnostic filter hides (MsgPack003 about the app's own type, C-2283-02).
notes: Fails on base with the crash from the issue (analyzer exception plus generator failure) and passes on the branch; it still passes when the new filter is removed, so the crash fix alone makes it pass.

steps.text: a library namespace `Lib` defines `partial record struct Item<T>` with one positional member `[property: Key(0)] string Key`
an app defines a record `Cmd` with a `[Key(1)]` member `Item<int> Member`, plus a resolver `AppResolver` marked `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver]`
`RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync` runs with expected resolver file `App.AppResolver.g.cs` and `LanguageVersion.Latest`
the helper first compiles the library source into a separate assembly `DefiningProject` and gives it to the app only as a metadata reference (no source)
the analyzers and generator run on the app with no expected diagnostics, so any diagnostic fails the test (the comment names the crash signs `AD0001` and `CS8785`)
a second, direct generator run must report nothing at `DiagnosticSeverity.Warning` or above (`Assert.Empty`) and its output must include a file named `expectedResolverHintName` (`Assert.Contains`)

does_not_check: It does not check the content of the generated code, or that the record struct member serializes at run time.
The type parameter `T` of `Item<T>` is never used by a member, so it does not test a member whose type depends on `T`.
notes: Fails on base with the crash from the issue and passes on the branch; it still passes when the new filter is removed.

steps.text: a library struct `MyGenericStruct<T>` marked `[MessagePackObject]` with a `[Key(0)]` member `Key` and a member `Unkeyed` that has no key attribute
an app class `MyObject` with a `[Key(0)]` member of type `MyGenericStruct<int>`, plus a resolver `MyResolver`
the helper compiles the library with a plain compiler call (`CreateCompilation` then `Emit`), so no analyzer ever reports the missing key in the library
the analyzers and generator run on the app with no expected diagnostics, so any diagnostic fails the test (the comment names the crash signs `AD0001` and `CS8785`)
a second, direct generator run must report nothing at `DiagnosticSeverity.Warning` or above (`Assert.Empty`) and its output must include a file named `expectedResolverHintName` (`Assert.Contains`)

does_not_check: It does not check that any assembly reports the missing key on `Unkeyed`; it requires the app build to stay silent about it.
It does not check the content of the generated code.
notes: Depends on the new diagnostic filter: with only the filter reverted it fails with two MsgPack004 diagnostics about `Unkeyed` (old-vs-new-tests.json, needs_filter: true). So beyond 'does not crash' it pins the dropped diagnostics that C-2283-02 refuses.
Fails on base with 3 diagnostics (analyzer exception, MsgPack004, generator failure).
